text:
Alexandre Carrier's season has a contract story running through it. The Quebec City native is headed for unrestricted free agency, The Athletic's Arpon Basu wrote on how he sees that future, and Dose.ca reported that wage negotiations have not begun.

On the ice, he's a 20 minute defenseman with 7 points through 21 games and 39 blocked shots. The five on five numbers are the concern: Montreal has held just 43% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, more than ten points below when he sits. Like Kaiden Guhle, he has been bailed out by finishing and goaltending, with goals on his shifts running about 8 better than the chances. His own offense is thin: 2 points in his last ten and almost no shots.

Last season was better. Evolving-Hockey put him at 0.7 wins above replacement, 88th among 215 defensemen with 500 minutes, most of it from even-strength offense. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found nothing far from typical either way.

For a player negotiating his next deal, the shot share matters more than the points. That is the number to watch.
